case_title: ROHIT BISHNOI v. THE STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.120B; Arms Act s.3, s.25, s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Honour killing, conspiracy to kill, use of weapon, involvement of multiple accused
neutral_facts: The accused, who were relatives of the deceased, were involved in an incident where the deceased was shot dead. The deceased was in an extra-marital live-in relationship with the sister-in-law of the accused. The accused were alleged to have conspired to kill the deceased and participated in his murder. The police investigation revealed that the accused had traced the deceased, conducted reconnaissance, and were seen on CCTV footage escaping the crime scene. The accused were arrested and charged with murder and conspiracy. The prosecution presented evidence including witness statements, CCTV footage, and recovered weapons. The trial court rejected the bail application, but the High Court granted bail, citing the testimony of a hostile witness. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, finding that the High Court did not consider the material aspects of the case and granted bail in a casual manner.
